item.title: State, city-parish officials hold ribbon-cutting ceremony for Pecue Lane project
item.description: ST. GEORGE &mdash; State and city-parish officials hosted a ribbon-cutting ceremony on Wednesday to celebrate the completion of the Pecue Lane project.Construction on the long-awaited road revamp wrapped up in February.The road now features a new diverging diamond interchange, where drivers switch to the opposite side of the road to accommodate turns onto the interstate. item.title: Governor Jeff Landry issues letter to school superintendents urging them to display 10 Commandments
item.description: BATON ROUGE - Governor Jeff Landry issued a letter to state superintendents urging them to display the Ten Commandments in classrooms following a ruling from the full U.S. Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals.The law in question, H.B. 71, was&nbsp;passed in 2024,&nbsp;mandates that a poster-sized display of the Ten Commandments in "large, easily readable font" be required in all public classrooms, from kindergarten to state-funded universities.&nbsp;"Posters have been donated at no public expense and

item.title: Louisiana lawmaker renews push for free breakfast in schools
item.description: BATON ROUGE - The fight against childhood hunger comes with a high price. One Louisiana lawmaker wants all public schools to serve free breakfast, but some worry about the cost.Statewide, about one in five kids live in a household where they don't know where their next meal will come from. item.title: Family members identify utility worker injured in Baton Rouge
item.description: BATON ROUGE - The family of a utility worker who&nbsp;fell from a bucket truck that caught fire Tuesday started a GoFundMe for him.It happened around 12 p.m. at the intersection of Evangeline Street and North Foster Drive. The worker, identified as Bevan Dupre by the GoFundMe, was taken to a hospital with burns in serious condition.His sister, Caroline, launched the fundraiser to support her brother and his family.Permalink| Comments

item.title: President of Hungary visits community settled by Hungarians outside of Albany
item.description: ALBANY - The president of Hungary visited a small community outside of Albany, which was first settled by Hungarian immigrants more than a century ago.The trip by Tamas Sulyok helps highlight the Hungarian culture in here in Louisiana. Doctor Carl Nehlig, president of the Hungarian Museum and Historical Society, says more than 200 families first settled in the area.Permalink| Comments
